newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Common Fund grant to boost African cotton trade.
newsitem.headline: Common Fund grant to boost African cotton trade.

text.p: The Common Fund for Commodities, a U.N. affiliate, said on Thursday it had approved a grant and loan of $9.3 million to improve cotton marketing in eastern and southern Africa.
The project, submitted by the Washington-based International Cotton Advisory Committee, will start in Uganda and Tanzania, with provisions for results dissemination throughout the region.
"The project will increase benefits from cotton production and marketing through the establishment of a transparent and efficient market system," the fund said in a statement.
The grant is intended to set up a market which "responds to producer and trader needs" by examining trade finance, a privately-run warehousing system and quality assurance, it said.
In addition to the Common Fund grants, contributions from governments to the scheme are expected to exceed $1.1 million and co-finance from local banks of $14.4 million is envisaged.

"The mitigation of risks, use of local inventory and warehouse receipts as collateral and strengthened capacity of local banks, will facilitate access to trade finance, improve the efficiency and reduce the costs of cotton marketing and trade," the fund said.
